# Build Artifacts

A successful build will produce the following artifacts in the same directory as the kernel.
By default this is `$MAKEOBJDIRPREFIX/path/to/sys/$KERNCONF/` and `$MAKEOBJDIRPREFIX` defaults to
`/usr/obj`.

* `rust_sysroot` directory
    * `libcore.rlib` - rust core crate built from the sources in the compiler repo
    * `libcompiler_builtins.rlib` - a dummy rlib required by the compiler
* `rust_sysroot_kmod` directory - same as `rust_sysroot` but built with PIC for ARM64 modules
* `bindings.rs` - declarations and type definitions generated by bindgen from bindings.h. Built into
                  the KPI crate.
* `bindgen_inlines.{c,o}` - source file generated by bindgen for static inline functions. This gets
                        built normally and linked into the kernel.
* `libkpi.rlib` - the KPI crate's code
* `rustroot.rs` - source file with one `extern crate` declaration per crate
* `rustroot.a` - the top-level static archive that gets linked into the kernel

For each crate `foo` added there will also be a `libfoo.rlib` in the build directory. Rlibs are just
static archives (.a files) with additional rust-specific metadata. This means that tools like
readelf, objdump and nm will work as usual. To demangle symbols these tools usually accept a `-C`
flag.

# Module Build Artifacts

Each module's build directory has its own `bindings.rs`, `bindgen_inlines.{c,o}`, `libkpi.rlib`,
`rustroot.rs`, `rustroot.a` and `libfoo.rlib` for each file in `RUST_SRCS`. These are not shared
with the kernel since the generated bindings.rs depends on the module's CFLAGS.

Note each rust module gets only the rust shims for its dependencies linked into it not the C
dependencies themselves. For example the rust virtio_snd.ko module depends on the C virtio.ko and
sound.ko modules. The rust side calls into these dependencies via libvirtio.rlib and libsound.rlib
which are both linked into virtio_snd.ko, but virtio.ko and sound.ko remain as separate modules.
This is fine for small shim libraries. To build a non-shim rust module and avoid linking a copy of
it into everything that depends on it the rust module must expose a C ABI.
